quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward means they are going to stop. Change your driving if you see this signal from the driver ahead of you.

questions.question: When parking, your vehicle must be visible for at least ____ in each direction.

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
200 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet
questions.explanation: Your parked vehicle must be visible for at least 200 feet in all directions. Only park where your vehicle will not block traffic.

questions.question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System loses traction on a slippery road, what should the driver do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle loses traction, press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically faster than you can. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes yourself will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Avoid tinted windows because they reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights causes your eyes to shrink. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the dark. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal means:

options.text: This is never used in traffic signals.
It has the same meaning as a red traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It has the same meaning as a red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road intersects with a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or barrier.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black lettering.
Shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. You may drive faster in good weather, but you should always slow down in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?

options.text: The safe speed for a residential area.
The safe speed for an expressway exit.
The safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for exiting a highway (in this example, 30 mph).

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 40 feet
25 feet
15 feet
20 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Parking too close can block emergency access and cause accidents.

questions.question: On a road with three or more lanes, a vehicle entering a lane from the right:

options.text: Always has the right-of-way.
Must yield to a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.
Should be given the right-of-way by a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.
Does not need to use its turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.
questions.explanation: On a road with three or more lanes moving in the same direction, a vehicle entering from the right must yield to a vehicle entering the same lane from the left.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on county roads next to public beaches is:

options.text: 55 mph
45 mph
15 mph
25 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph
questions.explanation: On county roads next to public beaches, the speed limit is 15 mph. Follow any posted speed limit signs that show a different speed.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction and drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means drivers cannot pass.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs mean:

options.text: School zones
No passing zones
Speed limits
Railroad crossings

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. The sign will have text that says 'no passing.'

questions.question: When you see this sign, it means:

options.text: There is an object on the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. Multiple chevron signs may be placed along a curve.

questions.question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:

options.text: Safe to cross because trains rarely come.
Dangerous
Safe places to park.
Places where you must stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer needs about 400 feet to stop from 55 mph.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward
At an intersection
At a stop sign
At a toll booth

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward
questions.explanation: Leave more space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. The vehicle in front may roll backward when traffic starts moving again.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road just before the exit lane
Once you see a toll booth
After you move into the exit lane
When you first see the exit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well before exiting. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic
Use the shoulder
Use the lane for oncoming traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane, two-way road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction the arrow points.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body process in one hour?

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
One alcoholic drink an hour.
Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink an hour.
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies process about one drink per hour. How fast alcohol affects you depends on the amount you drink, how quickly you drink it, your weight, food intake, and your health.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.
You can pass from the lane next to the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross quickly as fast as possible.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop for a train at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Wait until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not shift gears while crossing the tracks because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The larger vehicle.
The car on the left.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on wet or icy roads. Stopping distance also increases on surfaces with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road ahead has many turns or curves.
Traffic is increasing ahead.
There is a steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, slow down, avoid sudden braking or turns, and stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed the whole time.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a curve and speed up gradually as you leave it. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the least traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the most traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces oncoming traffic in the nearest lane.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm is raised upward, they are signaling that they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.
